## Multiple Choice Questions

**1.** For the Charles River invoice lines of fiscal 2026, the average line total is about half again as large as the median line total. What does this suggest about the distribution of line totals?

A.  It is symmetric, so the average and the median describe the typical line equally well.
B.  It is skewed to the right, with a minority of large lines pulling the average up.
C.  It is skewed to the left, with a minority of very small lines pulling the average down.
D.  It contains errors, because the average and the median of accounting data should be equal.

**2.** What is the difference between STDEV.S and STDEV.P?

A.  STDEV.S measures the spread around the median, while STDEV.P measures the spread around the mean.
B.  STDEV.S ignores blank cells in the range, while STDEV.P counts every blank cell as a zero.
C.  STDEV.S treats the values as a sample and divides by n − 1; STDEV.P treats them as a population and divides by n.
D.  STDEV.S works only on the columns of Excel Tables, while STDEV.P works on any range of cells.

**3.** An analyst wants the median line total of fiscal 2026 invoice lines only, and enters this formula:

```
=MEDIAN(FILTER(InvoiceLines[LineTotal],InvoiceLines[FiscalYear]=2026))
```

Why does the formula use FILTER?

A.  MEDIAN accepts no criteria, so FILTER supplies only the rows of fiscal 2026.
B.  FILTER converts the line totals from text into numbers first.
C.  FILTER removes the outliers that would otherwise distort the median.
D.  FILTER sorts the line totals into order, which MEDIAN requires.

**4.** A summary uses this formula, with the group name misspelled:

```
=SUMIFS(InvoiceLines[LineTotal],InvoiceLines[ItemGroup],"Furnture")
```

What does the formula return?

A.  The error #N/A, because no row of the Table matches the criterion
B.  The Furniture total, because SUMIFS corrects near matches in text
C.  The total of every row, because an invalid criterion is ignored
D.  Zero, without an error, which a comparison with a control total would reveal

**5.** In Tutorial 6.1, the revenue of the four product lines falls short of the fiscal 2026 control total by exactly the revenue of the Services item group. What does the difference show?

A.  The summary leaves out a category, and it is complete only when the category is added.
B.  The SUMIFS formulas of the four product lines contain a spelling error.
C.  The control total double-counts some invoice lines of the Services group.
D.  Services revenue should be excluded from the control total of the year.

**6.** An analyst wants to show how the fiscal 2026 invoice line totals are distributed: how many lines are small, how many are medium, and how many are large. Which chart suits the question best?

A.  A pie chart of revenue by item group
B.  A line chart of the line totals in invoice order
C.  A histogram of the line totals, in bins of equal width
D.  A stacked column chart of revenue by quarter

**7.** An analyst defines a PivotTable calculated field with the formula `=Quantity*UnitPrice` to show revenue. What does the field return for each cell of the PivotTable?

A.  The revenue of the cell, because the formula is applied to each row and the results are summed
B.  An error, because calculated fields cannot multiply two fields
C.  The average revenue per line in the cell
D.  The sum of the quantities multiplied by the sum of the unit prices, which is not the revenue

**8.** A PivotTable shows fiscal 2026 revenue with item groups in its rows and quarters in its columns. What does Show Values As % of Column Total display?

A.  Each quarter's share of the item group's revenue for the year
B.  Each item group's share of the quarter's revenue
C.  The change in each group's revenue from the previous quarter
D.  Each value's share of the revenue of all groups and quarters together

**9.** A formula on the Bridge worksheet refers to the PivotTable with GETPIVOTDATA:

```
=GETPIVOTDATA("Sum of Quantity",Drivers!$A$3,"Period","2026-Q3")
```

What is its advantage over a cell address such as `=Drivers!B5`?

A.  GETPIVOTDATA reads the value from the source Table, so the PivotTable can be deleted.
B.  GETPIVOTDATA refreshes the PivotTable every time the formula recalculates.
C.  It names the value by field and item, so it survives changes to the PivotTable's layout.
D.  GETPIVOTDATA rounds the value to the number format shown in the PivotTable.

**10.** An analyst adds a custom column to the InvoiceLines query and loads the query, but the new field does not appear in a PivotTable built from InvoiceLines. What is the most likely explanation?

A.  A PivotTable summarizes its own copy of the data, which updates only when it is refreshed.
B.  The custom column must first be converted to values in the Table.
C.  PivotTables cannot use any of the columns that Power Query adds.
D.  The PivotTable must be deleted and built again from the Table.

**11.** A PivotTable of the Charles River general ledger shows negative revenue for the Furniture account in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026. What is the most likely cause?

A.  Credit memos issued in the fourth quarter exceeded the invoices of the quarter.
B.  The Furniture Seasonal Promotion reduced the quarter's revenue below zero.
C.  The PivotTable sums the debits and the credits in the wrong columns.
D.  The year-end closing entry, which debits every revenue account, is included.

**12.** An analyst builds a trial balance at December 31, 2026, from GLEntry and leaves out the two 2026 closing entries. Why are they left out?

A.  The closing entries do not balance, so the trial balance would not balance.
B.  The closing entries zero the revenue and expense accounts, so the income statement could not be prepared.
C.  The closing entries are posted in fiscal 2027, after the cutoff.
D.  The closing entries hold the opening balances of the balance sheet accounts.

**13.** Why is the cost effect zero in the Furniture margin bridge of Tutorial 6.3?

A.  The Furniture product line has no cost of goods sold in the ledger.
B.  Costs are excluded from the bridge because they are recorded only in the ledger.
C.  Each item has one standard cost, so the same items cost the same in both quarters.
D.  The cost effect is always combined with the volume effect in a bridge.

**14.** From the third quarter to the fourth, the Furniture margin at standard cost falls, while the margin before promotional discounts rises slightly. What can you conclude?

A.  The decline comes from the promotional discounts, not from list prices, mix, or costs.
B.  The decline comes from higher standard costs of the Furniture items in the fourth quarter.
C.  The decline comes from a fall in the number of Furniture units sold in the fourth quarter.
D.  The two margins are calculated inconsistently, so no conclusion is possible.

**15.** Under the standard of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (PCAOB) on substantive analytical procedures, what should an auditor do before evaluating the difference between recorded revenue and an expectation?

A.  Ask management for the expected amount and accept it if it is close to the recorded one.
B.  Develop the expectation and decide in advance how large a difference is acceptable.
C.  Replace the expectation with the recorded amount of the previous year.
D.  Select a random sample of transactions, because analytical procedures use no expectations.
